analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (no code). Visible changes: the 'Last updated' date, GLM video documentation (variable-frame-rate tracks are now indexed with frame i timed at i / nominalFrameRate instead of refused with a 400), and a new paragraph (head lines 876-880) on rendering returned reasoning as reasoning_content and validating strict tools against their schema before exposure. I examined these against the threat model: T-041 (prefix cache, A-001) and TB-007. The docs still say media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture (head 830-831), so there is no new cross-tenant cache surface in the documentation. The doc keeps the bounds on decoded frames (512 MiB cap at head 815, 28,532 visual-token cap at head 828), the VisionMemoryGate reservation and deterministic 400s for processor refusals. The documented relaxation of variable-frame-rate refusal is a behavioral change in GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset that I cannot see. Its safety rests on those caps (frame-count and decoded-byte bounds under a VFR track). I cannot verify that the code enforces them, and a doc-only PR gives no evidence of regression. The next pass should confirm that the code change (if in the same PR) still enforces the decoded-frame cap and the token ceiling for VFR tracks, and that the strict-tool validation (ToolConstraintValidation.validate) fails closed. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation. I found no claims that weaken T-041/SEC-035 posture, attestation, or encryption.
